title: Google Opens 200-Task Multimodal Knowledge Agent Benchmark
summary: Google DeepMind releases Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark with 200 professional tasks across 10 verticals. Gemini 4 Carbon places second at 6x lower cost.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google DeepMind launched the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark with 200 professional tasks spanning 10 verticals and 83 occupations.
- Each task simulates three to eight hours of expert work, scored 75% on factual accuracy and 25% on visual design quality.
- Gemini 4 Carbon ranked second in quality while completing tasks at six times lower average cost than the top-scoring model.


Google DeepMind on November 10, 2026, released the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation framework designed to test AI agents on real-world professional tasks. Built in partnership with Artificial Analysis, the benchmark includes 200 tasks spanning 10 industry verticals and 83 distinct occupations, from architects and biologists to underwriters and data scientists. Each task represents the kind of multi-step project a seasoned professional might spend three to eight hours completing.


## Why Existing Benchmarks Fall Short


According to researchers Rohan Doshi and Ben Caine, most knowledge work benchmarks today are too text-heavy. "Most knowledge work benchmarks can be solved with text alone, without ever needing to look at an image or page layout," they write on the Google blog. "Yet, everyday professional work looks very different." The Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark addresses this gap by pairing realistic prompts with bundles of multimodal input files, including images, documents, and spreadsheets that mirror the complexity of actual workplace deliverables.


## How the Benchmark Works


Each of the 200 tasks comes with an expert-written rubric containing roughly 70 yes-or-no checks. Scoring is weighted 75% toward factual accuracy and 25% toward visual design quality, reflecting the dual demands of professional output. Every model tested runs inside the same open-source agent harness called Stirrup, which provides a shared toolset and turn budget to ensure fair comparison. Models tested on the harness showed extreme differences in efficiency, using between 30 and 130 turns on average to complete each task.


An agentic autorater grades outputs automatically. When domain experts reviewed the autorater's assessments, they agreed with its judgments 96% of the time, validating the scoring system's reliability.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 10, 2026, the full 200-task set remains private with Artificial Analysis to prevent training contamination. However, ten sample tasks are publicly available on Hugging Face for researchers and developers to explore. The benchmark is designed to evolve as professional AI use cases mature, with plans to expand coverage across additional occupations and industries.


## Gemini 4 Carbon Performance


Google DeepMind used the benchmark to evaluate Gemini 4 Carbon, which placed second in quality while completing tasks at six times lower cost on average than the top-scoring model. The company did not disclose which model claimed the top spot, but the cost efficiency of Gemini 4 Carbon positions it as a strong contender for enterprise deployments where both performance and budget matter. This release follows the wider Gemini 4 Carbon API rollout announced earlier the same day.


## What This Means


The Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark represents a significant step toward evaluating AI systems on tasks that more closely resemble real professional work. By requiring models to handle images, layouts, and multi-step reasoning simultaneously, it sets a higher bar than text-only benchmarks. For organizations exploring AI agent deployments across industries like finance, healthcare, architecture, and data science, this framework offers a clearer picture of which models can handle the complexity and multimodal demands of knowledge work at scale.
